utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Before we have the witness, we have two decisions to deliver. Yesterday this Trial Chamber received a request for an ex parte hearing from Defence counsel of Mr. Naletilic. The motion has been granted and we will hold the ex parte hearing today after 4.00 this afternoon. As for the rebuttal witnesses, according to the jurisprudence of the Tribunal, rebuttal evidence must relate to the significant issue arising directly out of the Defence evidence which could not reasonably have been anticipated, rather than to produce additional witnesses to reinforce its case. In a decision rendered by this Trial Chamber on the 20th September 2002, three areas of issues have been identified in the rebuttal case, namely, Sovici and Doljani events, wooden rifles and the Rados diary. According to this criteria, the testimony of Madam Plony Bos is allowed. As for the testimony of Mr. Prelec, so long as his testimony is within the scope of the above-mentioned three areas, his testimony is also allowed. It is so decided. Could we have the witness, please. Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yesterday I made a verbal request, and I don't know whether the Trial Chamber has reached a decision. I requested that the Prosecutor should be ordered to provide us with the closing brief in Croatian. I don't know whether the Trial Chamber has been deliberated on this matter, but if it hasn't, I'd be grateful if you could, because I am going to insist on this. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Par, for mentioning this element. We remember that you mentioned that very issue. We are doing some research at this moment in the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, and after that, I believe that we could give you a proper answer in that direction. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first of all, good morning. One thing isn't clear to me right now. I would be grateful if the Prosecutor could clarify the matter. The statement that we received from Mrs. Bos refers exclusively to those so-called wooden rifles and to nothing else. In the request that we recently received from the Prosecutor, the statement given by Ms. Bos, Plony Bos --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and the submission we received from the Prosecutor, we can see that according to that submission Ms. Bos can now testify. Your Honours, we can deal with this matter at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know the witness is here, but I'll be very brief. In terms of the issues that Mr. Par has raised and the Chamber has said it's doing some research on the issue, obviously the Prosecution would like to be heard prior to any decision being made on that. I'm concerned about a practice -- well, not a practice. I'm concerned that in the past couple of days the Defence have raised a number of issues which partly because of time constraints and, frankly, partly because of restraint on behalf of the Prosecution, the Prosecution is not being fully heard and before the Chamber would decide on these issues, we would certainly want to be heard. We certainly oppose the Defence request. We don't think it is the Tribunal jurisprudence. If the Chamber wishes to establish a briefing schedule on the matter, we would file a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I think we have known your positions on this very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It is cold here in The Hague, so be careful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Krsnik, the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, let me introduce myself. I'm Kresimir Krsnik. I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pleased to meet you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, since I know that you aren't used to being in a courtroom, I'm going to ask you to try and answer my questions by saying yes or no. I won't interrupt you. Just feel free to say what you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we first go into private session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we'll be protecting your identity. We're going to go into private session because there are a few questions I'd like to ask you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we're in open session again, so we have to be careful. You should be careful not to say your name, and I'll be careful too. We have to cooperate like this. We're in open session now. Everyone can hear what we are discussing. Tell me: Yesterday you said you guarded some machines. Who did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but what do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Who sent you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our superiors, the local authorities from the village, who were involved in negotiations sent us there. Negotiations were taking place at the time, and there was cooperation between the army and the HVO. And from the very beginning, when they started building the road, there were quite a lot of machines, private ones and company-owned machines. So they wanted security to be provided for these machines. They wanted them to be guarded overnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me: Do you know the name of the person who made you responsible for this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be so kind as to tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jure Groznica represented the HVO department and Dzemal Ovnovic was there and he represented the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They gave you that responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They agreed that there should be two Muslims there and two Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are a member of the BH army; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't belong to any one at the time, neither over there nor here. Only after they joined up at the very beginning, Stipe Pole enlisted me in the HVO, with Mr. Zelenika, Marko. So I was on the unit's list from then onwards, from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't a BH army member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't in any of the armies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's correct, but I had to be listed somewhere, registered somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me: Did you have a uniform and weapons? Were you issued with equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I personally had a uniform, but I didn't have any weapons, because there really weren't -- there really wasn't enough. And a colleague who was with me on the shift, he had a rifle, so the two of us, we were together, and we had one rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't there any -- weren't there any marks, any insignia on the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't any insignia, but very -- later on we were given patches, but I didn't sew them on. It said the 3rd Battalion, Mijat Tomic, but I kept this in my pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Mijat Tomic from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the BH army present in Sovici at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many members the BH army had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But approximately? You said that you spent your whole life in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know the exact number and I don't know who was registered as a member. I don't know who was not at all involved in all of this. In my opinion, there were over a hundred soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people come from Jablanica and Prozor, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no people from outside. Only later on, when there were some problems in Prozor, and then some people who were more or less refugees, they came over to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't receive any help from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom did that unit from Sovici belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It belonged to the command headquarters in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what that unit in Jablanica was called, or the staff, and who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what it was called. It was called the army, naturally. And I think the commander was Dlakic, Salim Dlakic something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Where were the BH army positions in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. They were somewhere up in the hill. I think they had two positions. But I never went up there. But I did go up there earlier on, so I knew those hills and the territory. They must have had two positions up there. And the HVO was holding positions near them, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it called Pasje Stijene or Povrsak, perhaps, if I could try to refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have Povrsak, a place called Povrsak, a place called Pasje Stijene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those the BH army positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. We had positions there, but I don't know whether that was the case or not. Maybe it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what -- why were they in danger. Why did they have positions up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Both sides took up position there in 1992, at the very beginning of the conflict, with the Serbian side. So they negotiated that if there was some sort of attack, if Chetniks came from Kupres, they should be there to defend the villages, and that's what they did, both the HVO and the army. They deployed there together and took up position as they saw fit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you believe in this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning, yes, until the very end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You believed. Tell me: Did you have a schedule of some kind, military occupational specialty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have a military occupational specialty, because I didn't serve in the former army, the former JNA either, so no, I never had such a thing. And even when I was on the HVO list, when I was registered with them, I haven't got any working experience which is recognised by anyone. The army calls these people Ustashas. When I go to see the Ustashas, they call me balija and so on. So throughout the entire period, my family was mistreated in Sovici, because I was on the list of a certain army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you perfectly. But you said that you weren't a member of any army, so I don't understand what you're saying now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was on the list, but I have nothing anywhere now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO list, from the time that we were made responsible for guarding these machines right up until the attack on Sovici, and then we were taken to the camp and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we know about that. We'll talk about that later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I left the camp, I wasn't -- I didn't belong to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you, but you said that some people would call you Ustashas. You mean they would call you yourself Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The people who lived with me before, the Muslims, and certain individuals from the commands too, would call me Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dzemal Ovnovic call you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't. Dzemal didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of relationship did you have with Dzemal Ovnovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as you're relationship was concerned, well, it was more or less normal, human. We never quarrelled. I never quarrelled with him, but I never really cooperated with him, and I don't to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he want to arrest you on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did he want to arrest you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are several reasons. It's not really ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could give us a few details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. It shocked me. I know you're right, but I don't want to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the same Dzemal Ovnovic who was the commander of the BH army in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to him after the arrest, or did your relationship cool?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we weren't really in touch all that much, not even before the arrest. His behaviour was somehow slightly different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise to counsel for the interruption, but I think it would be useful if we could know the time frame in which this arrest occurred, or the arrest that Mr. Krsnik is now asking about. I'm not sure whether it's in 1993 or in 1987, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Still we know next to nothing about this arrest. When did it happen, how, and where? Would you please clarify those issues for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. As you can see, that is exactly what I'm trying to do now, establish good communication with the witness. I'm not sure if this went down in the record, but the witness said that he refused to discuss this. It was out of politeness that I chose not to insist on certain details, but I will certainly at least ask you about the year in which this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please assist the Court, be so kind because we all want to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been somewhere in late 1992 or early 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether he came for you with the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we were not at home at that point because we were out doing labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me if that was the BH military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's something I don't quite understand. I think I am beginning to realise what this is all about, because yesterday I failed to understand the whole extent of it, I must admit. You said yesterday that you were not a member of the HVO, and you repeated this to me again today, that you were not a member of any of the different armies. Please let me finish. And a document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor yesterday, you said it was false and that you were never a member of the HVO but that your brother was, or something to that effect. Was your brother too a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Krsnik. I was listening to the evidence yesterday and again this morning, and unless the translation fails the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Court, I don't believe that was said. This man has said, over and over and over again, that he was on a list, an HVO list, because of the work which he carried out. He even had a uniform. He even had insignia for the Mijat Tomic 3rd Battalion, which he didn't wear; he kept in his pocket. How much clearer can he be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would be very grateful to you indeed. I've only just begun my cross-examination. Please, if you can just bear with me and see where I'm taking the witness to. We've only just begun to obtain certain clarifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I don't in any way want to constrain your cross-examination, but you must be fair, and that's our function here, to make sure that people are fair. You cannot say to this witness that he said something which he clearly didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour, but that was never my intention to begin with. All this time, you remember my objections to the Prosecution. I always say that you can't claim something that isn't grounded in anything. Do you think I would try something like that myself? No. Your Honour, please bear with me, and you will soon see why I am driving this witness down this road, very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, you have to drive on the right side of the road. I bear in mind that sometimes translations are difficult, but certainly it seems to me, and I think to the Prosecution and to the rest of the Bench, that you were putting something to the witness that he didn't say. That's all. Now, I won't say any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm really not clear about this now. You've got me a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness. Excuse us. We'll continue shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues tell me - and we have the transcript too, so we can restate the question, what the witness said yesterday. He said he was formerly a member of the HVO but that he was not a member of the HVO. Is that what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member indeed, but I never joined any of the actions except the drill once. Something was to be done for the army or - let me specify - we were supposed to put up a privy somewhere out in the field and then we were supposed to block some windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I was saying. Please, Witness, believe me. I'll never insinuate anything you didn't say, and thank you for providing this clarification. But if that was also your role in the HVO - I was myself in the army, so I know what I'm talking about - you must have had some sort of task assigned to you there. Did you receive salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did receive salary for all those days that we spent guarding the machines, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: Was it by mistake that you were on the list in the HVO as more or less a sharpshooter, a sniper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe they did assign some roles and put it down with schedules, but this is nothing that I would know about. I was not really interested in this, let me tell you. All those actions, movements, military plans or codes. My father was very ill. He was bedridden back home, had been for two years. I wasn't interested in any of those other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you have walkie-talkies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me personally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never did, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we used to have one before. It was a very small, hand-held walkie-talkie. It was used by children to play, and we would take this with us when we went hunting. But that was before the 1990s. A neighbour of ours gave it to us. He was a hunter and he had worked in Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of those did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had five all together. I had one, two, but I never kept it at my place. I'd only keep it for the other person for several days, if I couldn't go hunting myself. Then somewhere else would go and they would come to my place and pick it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please consider this: What will you tell me now if I remind you of the statements you had given before? First of all, I have before me a statement that you gave on the 11th of January, 1996, to the AID in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think we can ascertain very soon whether this indeed is your signature. In that statement, you claim that you had been a member of the BH army since 1992, and in a statement you gave three months ago, and here before the investigators, you claimed that you were a member of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can show this to you, just to be fair, you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know exactly what was happening there. At the very beginning of the whole thing, they had my name on a list, although I never really had anything to do with that army, and I never went anywhere with them, and I was not familiar with anything. But after I had left the camp, immediately after I had left the camp --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, let's just take one thing at a time and let's just clarify all of the points. It's only fair to everyone, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher. [In English] Madam Registrar, would you be so kind? [Interpretation] This statement, we'll send copies to the booth. It's not a very long statement, so -- [In English] I would like to show him many parts of this -- yes, when I tell to you, then ... [Interpretation] Unfortunately, we only have the statement in Croatian, because when the Prosecution summoned this witness, we had no time left to do the translation. However, it's a very brief statement, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it would assist, this statement was disclosed by the Prosecution to the Defence, and we have an English translation, in fact. I don't know whether an English translation was disclosed or not, offhand, but if it would assist anyone, I have one with me, anyway, and we can make copies if it would assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Krsnik told us that it's a very short statement and that he was not going to use it very extensively. So I believe that, you know, we could rely on the translation in the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd be very happy indeed, and I thank my colleague, the Prosecutor, if the English version could be provided. It's about two, two and a half pages long, the statement. I will be using it, and I was going to tender it into evidence, in fact. Number 414. And I thank my colleague from the Prosecution again for his assistance with the English text, because we never had an English translation of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please proceed, and while the registrar will copy that English version for that statement at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could you please just first show the witness the bottom of each page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And witness, please answer: Is this your signature at the bottom of all of these pages here? You can see, bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have confirmed this by signing, and you say you have nothing further to add. So of course you are telling the truth in this statement, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling the truth in all of my statements, not only in this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please have a look, this statement here. You see this spot here: "I surrendered to HVO soldiers on the 17th," and so on. "We found there 50 members of the BH army." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain why in this and the other statement you made, you claimed you were a BH army member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning that you were a member of the BH army, not of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as soon as we were arrested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have the English version in my hand now, and I don't want to make any response -- certain response in front of the witness. I think it would be very useful if we had the English text in front of us if counsel is going to continue making the assertion that the statement says that the witness claimed he was a member of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have here the statement in English, so I would like to ask the usher to please give this to the Chamber. It was a statement given t to ICTY investigators. I know the translation is running behind a little bit, and I can see the looks on your faces, so please just bear with me, a little patience. This statement was given to the investigators. I have the statement in English. And on page 1, it clearly states -- here it is. So can I have this distributed, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is the statement given on the 9th of April, 2001 -- correction. 2002. Page 1 clearly states: "I too was a member of the army," et cetera. So you can have a look and see for yourselves. That's what I'm asking this witness. I'm not making this up. Why did he say that he was a member of the BH army and here he's telling us that he was an HVO member, in any capacity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this trial has been going on for quite a long time. We made a decision concerning using the document in the cross-examination, that is, before your cross-examination, please furnish us with all the documents you are going to use during the cross-examination so that at least this Chamber, the registrar, could be prepared for the necessary copies of those documents in order to facilitate the proceedings. But now we come across the issue that we don't have the documents at our hands. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for clarification, there are two statements. Until the very last remarks of counsel, we were talking about the statement dated the 11th of January, 1996 that was provided to the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's the statement that I offered to provide the English translation of. At the very -- within the last few moments now, counsel has referred to the other statement, which is in fact the statement provided to the OTP on the 9th of April, 2002. The original version of that statement is in English, but there are two, and so I think that it would help me, anyway, if counsel could stick with one, or at least inform us which one he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And by the way, I have the B/C/S translation of the second statement, which is the OTP statement, in the courtroom with me, if it would assist the witness in looking at that statement. Counsel comes to that point --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please allow me. Please, let us not create any more confusion than necessary. I have a very serious and important cross-examination here, and I know exactly what I'm doing. The Prosecution can stand up as often as they like, but that will not keep me from going through every single detail with this witness that I have envisaged. He has interrupted me exactly four times up to now. Please, put yourself in my shoes. It's very difficult to follow the thread of the cross-examination. As soon as we come to an area which the Prosecution doesn't like, problems arise. I wasn't going to show the witness any other statements today, apart from this one. I do have several of them prepared just in case, but the Prosecution did the same thing and he told me that he was laying an ambush for my witnesses, so he only gave me the statements a minute before the cross-examination began. So can I now continue my cross-examination, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, these statements were disclosed to the Defence well in advance of this morning's proceedings. What counsel just said is simply not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We know that. We know that. Let's not argue on this issue. Mr. Krsnik, since the first statement is being copied, would you please concentrate on the second statement, because we have already have the English translation at our hands. You may ask some questions on the second statement, and then later on, when we've got the English translation, you may come back to the first statement that was made in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please excuse us. You know, this is a courtroom, so this is the sort of discussion we usually have. So please don't get confused. First of all, I'd like to ask you the following question: You told us twice today that you had never given any statements after 1994. You said this twice. You also claim that you never gave a statement in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But here you see, it's your own signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Perhaps this statement was taken in Jablanica, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm reading from the transcript counsel's question, in which he puts to the witness the assertion that twice already today the witness had claimed that he had never given any statements after 1994. Now, that's false. The witness has already testified that he gave a statement, what he estimated to be some two to three months ago. He didn't disagree with counsel's assertion that a statement was in fact given in April of the year 2002. So again, I think counsel -- I'd request that counsel be more careful in the assertions, the characterisations of the witness's testimony, that he's then turning and putting back to the witness in a different form. It's simply not true what he's just said again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, please continue with your questions, but be careful of the -- not to mischaracterise what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have put my submission correctly, and I see that the Prosecution is very eager to keep rising all the time. They should just remain standing, because they keep having objections. I said the truth. The witness said that he had never given any statements to the police after 1994. The transcript is quite clear. That's as long as the translation is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll look into the transcript. You continue your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am very worried about this, because we've been studying transcripts, and you know well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you tell me: Did you tell me this morning, when I asked you about Mostar and Jablanica in 1994, that you never gave any further statements to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to the police, but three months ago, in Mostar, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. That's what you told me the first time around. Well, you see, but the Prosecution reacts to this and they tell me the opposite. But that was exactly what you said the first time around. You said no further statements to the police until my statement to the investigators three months ago. So I'm very glad to ask you this question, and we can now keep on working together, because the date here is 1996.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they put the statements together at some later stage, or much later even, because the way they took these statements, they only singled out several details, wrote them down on a separate sheet of paper and then had them typed later on. But this was not typed in my presence, typewritten in my presence. I was only called later to sign these statements, but I had never had a chance to read this statement, so I had no means to monitor what they actually wrote down. As far as this statement is concerned, they only took several details from me, wrote them down on just a common piece of paper, and then after a month, or more, I was called to sign these statements. But I had never even read them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people from the police who came to see me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told them the story, then they would leave, they would have a statement typewritten, without letting you read it and then they would bring it back to you to sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If this is the statement from Konjic, because I think that's probably the way it was done. Actually, I didn't give this statement at the police station. It was in a house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here it reads: "CSB Mostar, Security Services Centre, State Security Department in Mostar." It says: "Department of the State Security, Konjic."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the same thing, because I never went to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do believe you, but can you please help us with this: Here it reads -- you signed the three pages of this document, so where did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how long did they take to bring this statement back to you to look at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they took the statement in a house, maybe not the entire statement, so maybe at a later stage, in Jablanica or in Konjic, they put the statement together. So after a while I was called to sign this statement. But this here, they could have added anything, possibly even something different from what I had originally said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this their usual practice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this about me being a member or that I surrendered. I don't know anything about that. That's what they wrote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did tell the investigators the very same thing three months ago. In your statement, page number -- page 1, the first page of your statement: "I was a member of the army. It was part of my work obligation. My duty in the army was the maintenance and guarding of machinery," and so on and so forth. So even in your statement of three months ago, you claim you were a member of the BH army and not of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, when I was a member there, I'd be on a list as a member of the BH army, and that's how I ended up in prison, because my name was simply wrong. If my name was Mato, I would not be detained on that day probably, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do agree with you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I do not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just need a number of points clarified. Please don't get me wrong.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I'm getting you wrong. You quote here the beginning of some statement. I'm not really sure about anything any more after all the suffering that I've gone through. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That seems to be the problem, yes. That's why I'm trying to help everyone to reach the truth. You see, you have also stated, both during one of the hearings and also in the statement you gave to the investigators, that you surrendered at Stipe Pole's house. In the very first statement you gave to the AID, you said you were in front of a school building and that that was where you surrendered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I surrendered at Stipe Pole's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have the statement in front of you, so can you just please look at the fifth sentence of that statement. It reads: "After we had surrendered to HVO soldiers, they told us to go to the school building in Sovici and hand over our weapons there."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but since we didn't go in front of the school, they brought us to Stipe Pole's house. It reads clearly that we were told to go to the school building, but there was nothing. Nothing happened in front of the school building, but rather in front of Stipe Pole's house. It says clearly that we should go to the school building and hand over our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but look a bit further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking a bit further down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "In front of the school building, we found 50 members of the BH army who had surrendered earlier." After I surrendered my weapon," so that means you surrendered your weapon in front of the school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was in front of Stipe Pole's house. And what this means -- because actually, you can't tell the destination here. If you don't know where Stipe Pole's house is, you must understand that it's very close to the actual school building, perhaps 150 metres away. So if you're looking for someone who lives near the school building, you would be told, "Go look somewhere in the vicinity of the school building."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I do know where Stipe Pole's house is because I did go to Sovici myself. Is the small restaurant across the way still there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still often go there for a drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was exactly what I wanted to ask you now. So this restaurant is still open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me. Then it continues. Ivan Rogic, he ordered me to leave the group of prisoners. Then he cursed me," et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait. Wait a minute. And then you say that someone wanted to kill you, although in the statement that you gave to the investigator, the events were described in a different way with regard to the incident involving Ivica Tomic and Mate Krtic. But you told the investigators something quite different.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what you mean. I didn't mention these details. There are other details that I didn't mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not saying what you didn't mention. I'm talking about what you did mention. You mentioned the same detail, but you described the event in three different ways. For example, you said you were locked in a cellar with 70 other people in Stipe Pole's cellar. In the statement that you gave to the investigators, you say it was with 10 to 20 people, and in the first statement we don't know how many people there were. And now you are claiming -- well, we have three different versions. In the first version, you say that you remained in the cellar alone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why did you then tell investigators that you were all taken together to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all forced out, but I was forced out to the school a little later, maybe ten minutes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But see what you said in your statement: "After that, they threw me into the cellar with the other prisoners."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the school?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. In the cellar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when Mr. Tomic took me out to shoot me, and he wasn't allowed to by Mato Tomic [phoen]. That was in front of the house of Stipe Pole, not in front of the school, the exact spot where the cafe is now, but there was no cafe there at the time. There was a place where buses could turn around there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be so kind as to clarify what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't have to read it out. I'm very well aware of what I said. But perhaps certain details haven't been included in all the statements, or perhaps certain details vary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But look, these details are very important, because we must know the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally know what the truth is. I know about those details, because I was in the cellar. You weren't. And I lived through this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems that this conversation is too fast. It makes the interpretation very difficult to follow. Witness, I understand that you're eager to give your evidence, but whatever you said in this courtroom will be translated into the other two languages, that is, English and the French. We rely very much on the interpretation of your testimony. So please wait for a while after you hear the question, then answer it. Try to slow down a little bit. Mr. Krsnik, I believe that you know that already, yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've heard what the Judges have said. We speak the same language and that can create a problem. So could you please wait for me to finish my question and then I will wait for you to finish your answer, so that we don't get in each other's way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to read out what you said about the cellar now, so could you be so kind. Once I've read this out, you can say what you want: "After that, they threw me into the cellar with the other prisoners. At about 2300 hours, all the prisoners were taken to the school, and I was the only person left in Stipe Pole's cellar." And then you go on: "Around midnight --" so a minute ago we heard your fourth version, according to which it was ten minutes later. Yesterday you didn't mention that at all, or rather, you said that you had been taken to the school immediately. And now you are saying: "Around midnight, Ivan Rogic and Vicko Bozic and Andrija Groznica came to the cellar."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then they beat you, et cetera, et cetera. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you told the investigators from the Tribunal, what you said at the hearing yesterday, is not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me: What is true in this case, at the hearing yesterday and to investigators from the Tribunal, you said that someone wanted to decapitate you with an axe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the hearing, you said Tuta's soldiers, and in the statement you gave to investigators of the Tribunal, you said that the neighbour wanted to cut your head off. And this is what you said in the first statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: But sir, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll read it out and then you can tell me what's true. I just want you to decide what the truth is. You are the one who knows: "At about 1200 on the following day, I was taken to the smoking house, next to Pole Ivan's house, also known as Bilon." At the hearing you said a kitchen. In the statement given to the investigators, you said a school kitchen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a school kitchen. You're not right. I said Pole Ivan's kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said a summer kitchen. We could go back to that. And the Prosecutor immediately intervened and said smoking house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the smoking house or kitchen, someone calls it a summer kitchen, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I've never heard that a summer kitchen could be in a smoking house. There's smoke there, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, this is called a summer kitchen. You smoke meat there, and there is a fire there, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the statement that you gave to the investigators, this is what you said: "Tuta's people took me to the school kitchen, which my neighbour, Pole Ivan, and not Stipe, used, and they wanted to chop my head off. Two of Tuta's men put my head on a log, a log that was usually used for cutting up meat. A neighbour was preparing to kill me with an axe."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does it state that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's in the statement you gave on the 9th of April, 2002, and it is on page 2, at the bottom. It's the statement that you gave to the investigators three months ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I said neighbour. Well, we're all neighbours. I didn't say whether it was this neighbour or that neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Tuta's people your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Tuta's people, yes. But no, no. Tuta's people, they came there, but the neighbours, they were observers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is what you said in the first statement that you gave to the AID. You went to the smoking house, Pole Ivan's smoking house, and you were asked whether you had any weapons -- no, you were asked about weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "They told me to lie down on my stomach. There were five or six HVO soldiers who were around me, and I did not know them. And at the door to the smoking house, Stipe Kopilas was there and Juka Groznica."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Juka Groznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the soldiers had an axe in his hands.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm asking you: Is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you told the Tribunal's investigators and at the hearing yesterday is not true. We can't have three versions of the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the neighbour wasn't the person who had an axe in his hand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's why I'm asking you about this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The neighbours were sitting in front of that kitchen and they were observing what was happening there. They were observing what was being done to me. But in fact the observers incited them to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want us to agree on the truth so that we know what we're talking about. At the hearing yesterday, you said that Tuta's people wanted to use that axe on you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was mostly Tuta's people, because the neighbours, they were giving instructions, but the people from the side, whom we did not know, they were the people who were acting and maltreating us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we have three varying statements. Could you help all of us and say whether the unidentified soldier had the axe in his hands, or whether it was a neighbour. That's what it says in the statement that you gave to the investigators. Was a neighbour of yours holding the axe? And did a neighbour want to kill you, or were Tuta's people involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tuta's people, whom I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what it says in two of the statements is not true, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd like to know which two statements are incorrect. I simply don't know. Counsel is referring now to three statements. I only know about two. I know what was said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think one is the neighbour of the witness holding the axe; another is the identified soldiers holding the axe; the last one is Tuta's people involved. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. At the hearing, the witness said that Tuta's people were involved. It was stated yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the statement given on the -- in April 2002 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ask the witness which two statements is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what I've been asking the witness all the time, and the Prosecutor keeps interrupting me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you can see how long it takes us to get to the real issue. Could you tell me now: Is it correct to say that a neighbour was preparing to kill you with an axe? This is in the statement that you gave to the investigators. It's on page 3 of the statement that you gave to the Prosecution from this Tribunal. That's not true then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If it had been a neighbour, I would have named him, and I would have named the man if I had known him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let's try and make this brief. You mean to say that it's not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That a neighbour was preparing to kill you with an axe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think you're going a bit too far with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell me whether it's true.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: A neighbour did not have an axe in his hands. Tuta's soldiers were. The neighbour was an observer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute, then. I'm just trying to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It seems to me, although it's going so fast, but it seems to me that counsel is not giving the witness a fair opportunity to respond to his questions before the next question comes flying at him, and that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I have the same feeling, Mr. Krsnik. Just go step by step, and slowly, so that we can know which two statements are not true. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. Mr. Krsnik, I'm trying to keep up with you, and I have my note of what this witness said yesterday in relation to this particular incident, and I have the two statements, and I have difficulty in finding, but I'm sure you'll direct me, to the passage, any part of the statements which says that the neighbour had the axe. Everything I see suggests that soldiers had the axe, while the neighbours were watching. I think you're putting to this witness -- Judge Liu has shown it to me. Judge Liu, I'm looking at. Okay. Judge Liu has shown me the passage you're referring to. Go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness, as you can see, we have now agreed that what you said to the investigators is not true. But in the statement that you have in front of you, halfway through, in the statement that you gave to the AID, you said --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know what I said and what I experienced, but perhaps a few things differ. But I'm not here to lie or to accuse anyone of having done something that that person did not do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this is what I'm worried about, because in 1996, you know, your memory was still fresh.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my memory isn't fresh even today, after all of the traumas. It can't be fresh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what is worrying me, Witness? And I'd be grateful if you could help me, you know. How is that that in 1996 you named each soldier, whom you knew, whereas for those you did not know, you said that you didn't know those soldiers, but you never mentioned Mr. Tuta? That's what worries me, and this is why I want to discuss this matter with you. I hope I'm behaving in a civilised way.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's really nothing I could say about Mr. Tuta, because I only saw him on one occasion, and I have nothing to say about him. I said that I saw him on that day and that I never saw him after that, so there's nothing I could add about the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, be honest. Are you sure that it was Tuta or did someone else tell you that was Tuta? Tell us honestly: Could you claim that you know this personally, for sure, or were you told -- is this something someone told you later on in a camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That it was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Tuta was there on that day when we were there. I don't know if he was there later on, because we were detained there, and the local people, our local people, our neighbours, the soldiers, and others, they came and said, "You'll see him now. That's Tuta." Tuta entered the school. They let him have an office, which was used by the teachers there. There were some other people there whom I really do not know. And this is where they questioned soldiers, et cetera, et cetera. I really didn't go in there. I wasn't questioned, and I have nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But what I want to ask you, and I will repeat this question: Do you personally know this as a fact or were you told about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people, soldiers, told me about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't personally -- you didn't personally know that that was Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he entered, that was the first time I saw him. I had heard about him before, but I had never seen him before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me: How tall are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: One metre and 82 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How tall was this person, the person whom you call Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was perhaps as tall as I am, and maybe even taller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be so kind to stand up? Could you stand up so that I can see how tall you are? If Tuta was even taller than you, I would like you to stand up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think that may raise a problem with the facial distortion, Mr. President. That's the concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we understand so. We know how tall 1 metre and 82 centimetres is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me: How tall am I, in your opinion? Am I a lot shorter than you? Can I ask you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe 1 metre, 75, 1 metre 76, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, give or take a centimetre. And what if I tell you that Mr. Tuta is as tall as I am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So the person who was as tall as you, or perhaps even taller than you, does this cast doubt on what other people said, on what people said about this person being Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you want to say that Tuta wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. Do you know why I want you to say this? Because you never stated such a thing until June in the year 2000. Just a minute. We will come to all of these issues. In the first statement, you said nothing about this. What you said to the investigators doesn't include anything about Tuta or the person whom you called Tuta. It says nothing about Tuta receiving an office in which he could question people. This is not something that you said in April of this year. So just a few months ago. And this is something that you're claiming at the hearing now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that was left out, but that's in fact what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you tell me -- could you describe Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Cikota was about your height, his hair was short, he had fair hair. He was well built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you said. Cikota was short, he had fair hair, and he was plump. Are you sure that was Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his men called him by that name, and that's who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, look. Cikota was 2 metres and 5 centimetres tall. Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the question on the grounds there's no basis -- there's nothing in evidence on that fact, and I think counsel is not qualified to testify himself on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has testified. If you check the transcript to see what the witness has said when I asked him how tall Cikota was and what he looked like. These are well-known things, you know. Don't make me ask for an exhumation in order to determine this, because it's very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How tall Cikota is is not established. We don't know how tall Cikota is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witnesses we have questioned have stated this. Unfortunately, we can't determine the issue if we don't carry out an exhumation, so we have to rely on people who knew him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, given that this person is deceased, this is senseless.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll continue. You said a minute ago that after that point in time you never saw Tuta again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nowhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you see that you did see him after all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't see him in person after that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see him on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps once or twice. I don't really watch TV. I haven't got much free time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there's an interesting detail here. You said, later on, while he was in hospital in Zagreb, before he was transferred to The Hague, "I saw him on television." How could you have seen him on television given that he was in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they showed him in the hospital, and even before he went to hospital, he appeared on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But no. Here you quite clearly state that it was while he was in hospital, and I'm claiming that Mr. Tuta was never shown on television while he was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but I did see him. There was something to do with the hospital, or it was around the hospital, or while leaving the hospital, but I did see him. That's the main point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's carry on. Would you be so kind as to help us clarify a matter, help us see what the truth is. You know when you were taken behind the house and tied there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, behind the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the first statement, we have your second statement, and we have what you said at the hearing. Here you say: "They ordered me to get up from the smoking house. They took me behind the school. They tied my hands behind my back and they ordered me to lie down on my stomach."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were some other friends there, but you say: "This is where I saw --" and you name the person -- "Stipo Kopilas, Juko Groznica, Ivan Kolak."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "But I don't know whether they beat them --" and you're referring to the people you saw there, "-- because when I got there, no one was beating them any more. Half an hour later, one soldier untied my hands and ordered me to untie the hands of the others."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they weren't Tuta's people, Tuta's men. It's not correct what you stated yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were Tuta's people on the side, but there were people from Posusje too. There were a lot of people I knew, people who visited me at my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me: Who are Tuta's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people like us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that they were Tuta's men? Did it say Tuta's men or Tutici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It said the "Convicts' Battalion," and then the other local soldiers called them Tutici, or Tuta's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell us: You didn't mention the Convicts' Battalion in the first statement or in the statement that you gave to the investigators and you didn't mention it at the hearing yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no one asked me about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise. The translation indicates counsel just said that -- put to the witness that he did not mention Convicts' Battalion at the hearing yesterday, and I think again that's a bit of a mischaracterisation of the evidence that's been put to the witness. I think the witness quite clearly talked about a number of units, including this one, in his testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think today the witness also said -- he said that Convicts' Battalion and then the other local soldiers called him Tutici, or Tuta's men. It's quite clear in the transcript. Mr. Krsnik, could we stop here and continue after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but I'm still claiming that the witness didn't mention the Convicts' Battalion yesterday, and similarly, he hasn't mentioned it right up until now. My colleague the Prosecutor is not right. And this is the first time he has mentioned it in response to my question. Thank you. We can have a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, anyway, we'll look into the transcript. We will adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us please continue. Witness, could you please tell me: At what time of day exactly Mr. Ivan Rogic was reading this so-called conviction, according to your statements?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the witness's microphone please be turned on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your microphone is not turned on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to repeat your answer, because the microphone wasn't on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know exactly what time it was, but it may have been between 3.00 and 5.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us: What time did the bus for Ljubuski leave? What time of that day or night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at dusk. It was in the evening, almost night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you this is the following: In your first statement, the one you have in front of you, you mentioned that only Mr. Rogic was there, and you claim he read out to you some sort of a sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before you got onto the bus. Now, what is the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because in the second statement, you say that Rogic was there and that he came with Tuta's deputy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, outside the school building, and there were other people there. I don't know who exactly. But I was there for the whole day, and I was maltreated, so I could hardly see the people around me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm putting to you. Is it the case that Mr. Rogic read this out to you before you got onto the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, outside the school building. They had us lined up there and he began reading it, but he didn't finish because he was interrupted by someone, who told him, "Don't read this." And then they took us to Stipe Pole's house. They put us onto the bus and took us to Doljani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you see, you said just a while ago that it was about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon and that you took the bus in the evening, at dusk, you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was spring, you know, so night began to fall at a very early hour. So after 4.00 it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you see, in the statement you gave to the investigators of this Tribunal, you claim, "Later on, after that sentence was read out, the same night they put us onto the bus, which took us through Doljani and through the woods towards Risovac, and at dawn we arrived in Ljubuski. That was on the 18th of April." So was it on the 18th of April that you arrived in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The morning of the 18th or the morning of the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, we spent the night of the 17th and the whole day of the 18th at the school building, and this happened on the morning of the 19th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this statement should be corrected. It shouldn't read the 18th, but rather the 19th. Well, anyway, let us go on. In your first statement, it says, "Ivan Rogic," and then immediately we were put onto the bus. And then you continue. You make no reference whatsoever to people who were with you on the bus, that is, no reference to anyone aside from HVO soldiers who were in the bus, and you were supposed to report to them every 15 minutes, that is, to these soldiers who were with you in the bus, and you never said a single word about anyone maltreating you in the bus, or anyone else, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one maltreated me. And as for the others, there was Dzemo sitting up front, and the people who were sitting next to Dzemo, they kept beating them all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm not asking you about Dzemo. I'm asking about you. Because at the hearing, and here, you said something completely different.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I said is that all those who were sitting in the front part of the bus were being beaten and maltreated, and I was sitting at the back of the bus. And no one maltreated me, except I had to report every 15 minutes to declare my presence, that sort of thing. The bus would stop over at every checkpoint, and they checked us at the door, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an HVO military police presence in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't it the military police who took you on that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who belonged to which unit, but I do clearly remember a man named Robi, and there were other people with him, and there was a jeep just ahead of the bus. It was dark, so we couldn't see really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But did you see the military police at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether they were members of the military police or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of this man named Robi, I would ask Your Honours to please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us: How did you surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: How did I surrender?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Who told you to surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, I'm not sure how to explain this.
