We did not really surrender, because, after all, the shooting and the explosions, there was a lull for a while, as though nothing ever happened, and between all those moments, two soldiers came up to us, soldiers from Posusje, soldiers I had known from before --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please excuse my interruption. Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know their names, but I'm not willing to say their names. I know both their first and last names. They used to come to see us before, and we were friends, good friends. They came to us to have coffee with us, and we had to make them coffee, and they had a laugh. They said, "We're here now for you to hand over the weapons you have. All those who are in possession of weapons should hand them over right now, and nothing will happen to any of the people who do." Mr. Dzemo and Tuta are negotiating at Sovicka Vrata, so if there are any such people, they should come down to the school building, and when we arrive there. They said not the school building. Stipe Pole's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the third version of the events we're talking about, and now I'll tell you about the first two, the ones you gave yesterday in your statement to the investigators. You claimed the following: "After a while, I got out of the house to see what was happening."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It was interesting. After all the shooting, not to come out of the house to see what was happening would have been strange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I then saw two HVO soldiers head towards the house." [redacted] [redacted] I said yes. I asked them why they were shooting, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. They weren't the ones who were shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this is a protected witness. We will have the relevant part redacted. But be careful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, but this would have been difficult to avoid, for me, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have to be careful. I was only reading, so I got carried away slightly. After that, you go on to state that one of them was abusing you verbally and that politics was actually to blame for all of this. A very bad word is used here. I don't want to say it. And then you go on to say: "I don't know what that Croat's name was. He was a soldier from Posusje. He was wearing camouflage uniform with HVO insignia." Today you said that you did know what his name was but that you were not willing to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't want to say, and that's why before I said I didn't want to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why didn't you tell the investigators this same thing? However, in your first statement, you say the following: "HVO soldiers --" and you don't specify which HVO soldiers. "I surrendered to HVO soldiers on the 18th of April around 6.30 in the afternoon, in the hamlet of Celici, together with my brothers," and so on and so forth. Now, however, during the hearing, you said -- I'll read the precise line to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're mistaken there a bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're here to correct me, please. You say the following, page 24, line 1 -- actually, starting from page 23, line 23, 24, 25. The Prosecutor asked you the following question: "Who was the local commander of the BH army in Sovici?" Your answer was "Dzemal Ovnovic." "Do you know what he did at that time?" And then you say "He, Dzemal Ovnovic, in person, informed the inhabitants of the village that they were supposed to hand over their weapons. He promised that nothing would happen to us and that he had personally negotiated this with Tuta." Now, there are three different versions. Did this unidentified soldier from Posusje tell you about Tuta and Ovnovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you said at the hearing is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: After five or ten minutes, maybe half an hour, within his arrival, they went around the village with a megaphone and they were informing people about this, but I had found out from the soldiers about this even before that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see that my learned colleague is looking for this spot in the transcript. It's line 23, 24, 25, page 24, line 1. So it is true that the soldiers from Posusje told you about negotiations, and not Dzemal Ovnovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could we please clarify something about the people you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. refer to as Tuta's men? What were they wearing? Because in the different versions, the one you gave to the investigators and what you actually said at the hearing, we established that you made no reference to them in your first statement, aside from a very interesting detail that I will ask you about later on. So can you please finally tell us: What were they wearing, Tuta's men, to help you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of different soldiers there wearing different uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies, but I'm asking you about Tuta's men. You remember what you said at the hearing yesterday, that they were wearing different clothes from anyone else there and that that was how you recognised them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing black uniforms and there was another team of men who were wearing different camouflage uniforms, and there were yet other people wearing camouflage uniforms, olive-drab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do accept all of this, but I'm asking about Tuta's men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tuta's men were mostly wearing black uniforms, and there were other people there who --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That suffices for the time being. I'm only asking you about Tuta's men. In your statement to the investigators, you say the following. You speak about Tuta's men. This is page 4 of the Croatian version of the statement. You say they were wearing camouflage uniforms, and some of them were wearing black uniforms. Tuta himself was wearing a uniform that was greener than the other uniforms. What do you mean by "greener"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was different from the other uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not quite the military uniform I was familiar with. It was a bit -- a deeper shade of green. I'm not sure how to put this. It was a camouflage uniform, but it was greener somehow. The shape of the uniform was somewhat different from the other uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what difference there was between the uniforms worn by the HVO members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. There were some differences, but it depends on how you look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The BH army and the HVO wore almost the same uniforms. That's what I'm putting to you. And now how can you tell which soldier belonged to which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they wore insignia on their shoulder straps, on their pockets. It depends. Some had no insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those wearing black uniforms, you are sure that those were Tuta's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure. There must have been a lot of his men wearing black uniforms. Not all of them, perhaps, but quite many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One just didn't talk to them, because they were beating people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that your conclusion, that those were Tuta's men? How did you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you already that I could tell because of the insignia and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I accept everything you say, Witness. There's no need to get upset. Let us try to calm the situation down a bit. There is no need to get upset over this. Those wearing camouflage uniforms, as you say in your statement to the investigators, how could you tell that those were Tuta's men? Did you talk to them, those people wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really talk to them. I only talked to those people I knew from Posusje, but to those other people, I had no contact with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those from Posusje, were they Tuta's men too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really, at least not the ones I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you say so in your first statement? Because you specify whom you knew and whom you didn't know, and you say the following in your statement: "I have read the statement. I hereby confirm with my own signature that all my statements were recorded authentically. Should I remember any further details, I am prepared to provide them." In the period between 1996 and 2002, you made no further statements, and apparently you've had no further recollections, and you confirmed the authenticity of the statement with your signature. You named every single soldier, and if you didn't know a soldier's name, you said "unidentified soldiers." How can you explain this to me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's easy. Those who were beating me, I specified who they were; and those others whose treatment was correct, I will never say their first or last names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, but Tuta's men are apparently not among them, because that's exactly what you said. And you did name the ones who had beaten you, but no Tuta there, or Tuta's men. They're not included. It's exactly what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, I didn't know any of his men by the name. I only knew a neighbour who was with Tuta, but not the rest of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, the reason I'm asking about this is because there is a very interesting detail in your statement on page 2, your statement to the AID, the one you have before you, because that's the statement I'm referring to most of the time. In that statement, you seem to know who Tuta's men were, but you did not put them in Sovici. It says: "Those were members of Tuta's unit whom I knew by sight. They were billeted in the barracks at Heliodrom." You see that you knew back then, and you did refer to those people, but you never put them in Sovici in any one of your sentences.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those people who were in Sovici were the same people who lived at Heliodrom. I saw them there many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a moment. You state very clearly here that you knew them by sight because they were accommodated at Heliodrom. So you state very clearly where you knew them from. But let us not delve any further into this. Let me ask you the following. Let us try to clarify a couple of other issues. Could you please tell me why, who, and were you at all at Risovac for military training, and what sort of training was it, if there ever was one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: This training, yes, there were training sessions, but I didn't know anything about that, because I had been summoned a day or two before the Bajram, Muslim holiday. And I was angry that they were calling me at that time. And it may have been some sort of a test to see how confidential I was, but I always welcomed all those who were well-meaning persons. But even though it was just before the Muslim holiday, I decided to go, and when I arrived, I was given certain assignments, and several soldiers were with me and we were supposed to put up a privy, a field water closet. And then we were ordered to chop up some wood and load it onto the truck in the morning to protect the command building somewhere in Jablanica. In the morning, the truck was there and we loaded this onto the truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Was this what you refer to as "training," you using a chainsaw to chop wood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was my assignment, and we loaded this wood onto the truck in the evening. And Stipo Kopilas and some other local commanders arrived in the evening and they told me to get ready and go back home because it was a holiday and that I should be at home and that I was no longer supposed to come there. So I left. I invited people over to have coffee at my place whenever they could. Goodbye, goodbye, we said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you will surely agree with me that this was no military training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this training I went to, and I never returned, there was never any other training apart from this at any later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I read through your first statement, if I follow it correctly, you spent very little time in the school, almost no time at all. How can you know what happened in the school if you weren't there, or if you only spent very little time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was taken into the school and out of the school on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, but on the basis of your statement, the first one and the second one too, it is very clear, it's quite possible to determine how much time you spent in the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe no time at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you state very clearly when you left the cellar, when you were taken to the smoking house. You clearly state when they took you behind the house and when you set off for Ljubuski too, of course. So I'm asking you where you obtained all these details from, and especially a detail that you haven't mentioned in any of your statements. And how is it that you know that Tuta was even provided with an office? And I asked you where the office -- where his office was, whether on the ground floor or on the floor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you had been in Sovici, you would have seen this. The offices were on the floor, not on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you say "on the floor." To the left and to the right there were two big classrooms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and two big offices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you see that? Where were you? How is it possible for you to see all of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Can you tell me the name of one person who was questioned by Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he questioned quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Give me a name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it really necessary to give you a name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone you like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to mention anyone, but if I started mentioning people, I'd have to mention quite a few names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know why I'm asking you this? We've questioned quite a few people who were in the school before you, you know. Just a minute. Just a minute. I'll speak very slowly now for the sake of the interpretation and for the sake of my learned colleague, the Prosecutor. None of the witnesses said that they had seen Mr. Tuta in front of the school or in the school?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We disagree with that assertion, Mr. President. It's not the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's why I said this very slowly. I emphasised this because I knew what the reaction would be. I'm only speaking about the school and what happened before the school. Believe me, I know each statement by heart. I've spent two years here already. I'm only speaking about the school and about the place in front of the school. But nevertheless, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What will you say if I said that we heard testimony here, and I can't mention any names, but I would like to tell you that all the witnesses - and that's how I'll call them in order to protect them - none of them claimed that Dzemo Ovnovic surrendered to Tuta or negotiated him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not -- that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I claim; that's what witnesses have claimed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who claimed that were lying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were BH army members, you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they're all lying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If anyone said that, said that he didn't go up there and didn't negotiate with him, if anyone said that, that person is lying. And if anyone said that he wasn't provided with a car to get away from Jablanica and was then returned from Doljani, if anyone said that, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was he given a car to go to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to this form of questioning, and would also direct the Trial Chamber to the testimony of Witness Y on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, when you quote the testimony of a witness, please be very careful about that. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I would just like to say that we're talking about Witness Y, Witness Y must know the best. He claimed the exact opposite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he get a car to go to Jablanica? Did the HVO give him this car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local commander, Jure Groznica, gave it to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have some kind of an agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were related. One of them was the best man. That was the main thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you want to say that the BH army betrayed Dzemo Ovnovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to say anything, because we didn't fight for someone to betray the army or the HVO. These are other matters, and little people don't know anything about this. That's how things had to pass. We all suffered. It doesn't matter who. People suffered on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you, absolutely. Don't get angry, but I have to ask you about certain things that have to do with Mr. Tuta. Please be patient and assist me. I'm defending my client. You must understand this. In the statement that you gave to the investigators, today you told me that Rogic was interrupted by someone in his speech, that someone interrupted him, and here you quite clearly stated who interrupted him. It was this person called Cikota, who was a short person, a little fat, with fair hair. But what is interesting in what you say is that "while Rogic was speaking to us in the yard, I saw Tuta," et cetera. "They were only 5 metres away from Rogic. So Tuta must have heard what Rogic was saying." And that's all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not must have heard; he could have heard. You say that you are defending Tuta. You really are right. But where were you in 1993, when it was necessary to defend all of us, when Mr. Tuta came to beat us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look, if I had been there in 1993, believe me, I would have defended all of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't talk about everything, sir, but I've lived through all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm very sorry about that, you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is what I have just said, and I said this because I want you to understand that the situation is different now and that I have to insist on certain matters. But if I'm tiring you, I can stop. It's really not a problem.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, very well. You've gone a bit too far, but it doesn't matter. I'll carry on listening to you a bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry. I didn't think I had gone too far, but I really will try not to disturb you, not to tire you. I'm just reading out what is stated here. I'm not inventing anything. And you signed both statements, you read them through, and you signed them. That's why I'm reading from them, so as to prevent you from misunderstanding certain issues. The document which the Prosecutor showed you at the end, yesterday, naturally you said that you had never seen that document. But when you came to The Hague, did the Prosecutor show it to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And to be more specific with regard to this document, the first time I heard about some parts of this document, I heard it on the local TV in Jablanica, from 1994, when I had left the camp. I heard things being read out on the Jablanica TV. But I had never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the local TV station called Press Service of the 44th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the name was exactly, what it was called exactly. It was some kind of cable TV. It still exists today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, look, we've got a lot of cassettes from that TV, and it was called the Press Service of the 44th Mountain Brigade, and it was part of the BH army from Sovici. It's a local brigade, under the command of Enes Kovacevic in Jablanica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was read out on that TV station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yesterday you said that you didn't know that man and that you had never heard about that document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have heard about the document, but I said that I had never had it in my hands before, but I heard about it when I left the camp, maybe several months later. I don't know exactly when. But I didn't have a TV and I didn't really go to other people's houses, but I just happened to be somewhere when the news was on, and this was read out once or twice. I don't exactly remember what was read out, and I wasn't really interested in it then. And yesterday, what I read out -- I don't know. There was just a part that I read at the beginning, two or three sentences that concerned the training in Risovac, but I didn't read anything further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said in that notorious document, you said that you had had problems, but now you say that you didn't have problems. So it's not correct what is stated in there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecutor said this yesterday. I can read it out to you. I don't want to waste any time, but I can read out what it states. When you were asked whether you had had any problems because you were a member of the HVO, because you and your brother were in the HVO, you replied that you had -- didn't have any problems.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "problems"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you had problems with other Muslims, with your neighbours, inhabitants of your village, because you were in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. The question is related to whether, as indicated in the document, he had any problems in the HVO because he had brothers who were members of the ABiH. That was the question that was put to the witness, for which there's a basis in the document itself, not the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Okay. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In the transcript we see that because you and your brother were in the HVO. That's a totally different assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but we've got the document here, and this is what I said. If I have understood this correctly, in the document it says that he had problems with his Muslims, that he and his brother had problems with other Muslims because they were HVO members. If I have made a mistake, please correct me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have made a mistake, sir, because up until then, I didn't have any problems, up until the time when I was taken to the camp. Then I had traumatic experiences in the camp, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: But up until the time when we were locked up, we didn't have any problems. No one was bothered by the fact that we were there. And there were other people there too. I wasn't the only one there. There were other Muslims who were members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't have any problems because your other brothers were in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what it states here is not correct; is that right? I have read out what it says in the document. In the English version -- it's page 43 in the English version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: But, Mr. Krsnik, I think he said yesterday, if we're talking about the same passage, when the passage was read out to him, he said that he was unaware of these suspicions and feelings expressed in the document. He was unaware when he was with the HVO that he was treated with suspicion because he was a Muslim. That's what he said yesterday. He can't answer for what the person's suspicions were, but he said yesterday that at the time he was unaware that there was any bad feeling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Judge Clark. He has confirmed that. Not that he was aware of that, but it confirms the fact that there were no problems. This is what he just said a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm looking at the statement that you gave to the investigators. Is it correct when it says that after negotiations with Sefer Halilovic, rather, when Sefer Halilovic came to negotiate with SFOR - this is on page 3 - is it true to say that it was agreed that civilians should be taken by bus to Jablanica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object on two grounds, Mr. President. These are events that occurred after the witness had been removed from Sovici. It's therefore beyond the scope of his direct examination. Secondly, this is an issue that falls beyond the scope, I think, of the Trial Chamber's ruling on the purpose of this particular witness's rebuttal testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, you understand that this is a cross-examination. The Defence counsel has the right to challenge the credibility of this witness. But, Mr. Krsnik, I thought you were touching upon the Rados diary a moment ago, that you'd come back to that issue. Would you please tell me how long are you going to last in your cross-examination? It has been going on for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have almost finished. But when we're going through documents, or parts of this document yesterday, I only went through what the witness said during the hearing, we were looking for events that -- of which the witness might have knowledge. For example, this refers to the last question. We then realised -- or rather, we know that after he was questioned yesterday, and we didn't know what the Prosecution's intentions were with regard to these issues, we knew that he couldn't know anything in a direct way because after the 18th there was nothing else, apart from the fact that he belonged to the army and the training, et cetera, and we went through these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may try your luck in that direction, but I'm not sure whether you can get the proper answer from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Mr. President. I'm looking at the questions and I think I'm approaching the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having conferred with my colleagues, I think we have covered all of the issues. We have touched on everything, on all the relevant areas. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I hope you don't mind my saying this to you. This witness was called as a rebuttal witness to deal with a very specific and concrete issue in relation to your client. You know what that issue is: His presence in Sovici on a particular date. Now, why don't you put, or why haven't you put to this witness what your case is so he can deal with it? Because it seems to me that it's fairer if it comes from you than if it comes from the Prosecution or from me. This witness is here to help the Court, and he may help your client. You won't get another chance, so why don't you put your case to this man?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for a very simple reason. There's nothing I want to hide from the witness. This is not a strategy I'm employing. I never have had such intentions. Your Honours, Judge Clark, when you read all these statements, it was quite clear to me what was at stake, and I don't see why one should go on. I did assert my thesis, but in an indirect manner. And what it says in the first statement that he made in 1996, with regard to this, my claim was quite clear. Had Tuta been there, he would have said so when his memory was still fresh, and that was in 1996 because on page 2, Judge Clark, and I'm going to suggest that this statement be tendered into evidence in any case, on the second page it is quite clear that this is the case, and especially after the description provided. Your Honours, we know that Mr. Tuta is not one metre and 82 tall. So do I still have to cast doubt on certain matters, if the witness says that he is a metre 82 tall, or even taller --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, sir. I didn't -- I said I don't know whether he's shorter or taller, but about a metre and 82. I don't know whether he is taller or shorter than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but half an hour ago you said that Tuta was 1 metre and 82 centimetres tall, or even taller. We can check this in the transcript. You are now correcting yourself again and providing us with a fifth version. And Witness, please, could you look at me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I claim that Tuta and Cikota weren't in Sovici, for if they had been there, you would have said so in the first statement, immediately after the events.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, were you in Sovici on that day when the attack against Sovici was carried out? I was there, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. I'm here to put the questions, and you're here to answer. You know, let's not quarrel, you know. Because if you make a claim 12 years after the event, and in particular, 6 years after the event, and I'm claiming, and other people from your village gave testimony here: If Tuta had been there, you would have said that a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, sir. You're right. If you've finished --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I would just like to change my place so that I'm not standing behind the witness's back. Cross-examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, my name is Branko Seric. I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Vinko Martinovic. Yesterday you stated that you were arrested on the 17th of April, 1993, that you were taken to Ljubuski on the 18th, and to the Heliodrom one and a half months later. Could we agree that you got to the Heliodrom at the beginning of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. I can't remember the exact date, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. AF, are you a smoker?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: A smoker, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a smoker in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in front of the Heliodrom, and you spoke about this in the testament that Mr. Krsnik has referred to already, you said that you were lined up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree that they took everything away from you and from the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything. Our cigarettes, lighters, everything that we had on us, money too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree that you had to leave some of your clothes there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Anyone who had additional clothes in a bag had to leave them with the police, and they would then take them to a warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you keep your -- were you able to keep your lighter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when the International Red Cross visited the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember when that was exactly, but the visit took place later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I can't remember exactly, but the visit did take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to a question from the Prosecution, you said that on a certain day - you can't remember when - but it was in June or August, you were taken to the Bulevar, next to the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in the statement that you gave in April 2002, you said that it was in August. You were more specific than you were yesterday. What's correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. A lot of time has passed. But I do know that it was in the summer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the date. What I'm asking you is: Was it in July or in August? And you've already said that it was August in your statement to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, thereabouts. July or August. Was it late July or early August, I'm not sure, but it was summer, and days were hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be more precise? If you put this in relation to the visit by the International Red Cross, was that before or after the visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said MP Luka Stojanovski drove you there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please pause after my question for the benefit of the interpreters and then begin your answer. Are you familiar in which way the military police is related to Vinko Martinovic at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you that this man, Luka Stojanovski was never a member of Vinko Martinovic's unit, what will you tell me in response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't tell you anything. I never said he was a member of Mr. Martinovic's unit. But he drove us everywhere whenever we went to do force the labour. He drove us everywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecutor dated April 2002, only six months ago, you said that, first, you had been taken to the engineering faculty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct. They would often take us there. They would put us up there, and then soldiers would come and pick us up to take us to forced labour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you -- that from the medical faculty you were taken near the medical centre and close to the place where the new church is, next to the kindergarten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new church is not exactly in the vicinity of the kindergarten. Like I said, next to the medical centre there is a kindergarten indeed nearby. And there is a church somewhere in the area, and there's a park just above. And like I said before, there is a playground, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but please, just say "correct" or "not correct."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness photographs 14.5 and 14.4. This is 14.4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this photograph, can you see the engineering faculty in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out in this photograph, please, the exact spot that you were taken to from the engineering faculty, which you said was near the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Should I point it out? Should I make a sign on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please use the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we were taken to where these houses are, right here. That's where they took us to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark this with number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you please point out the kindergarten.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's right here. I'm not sure when this photograph was taken, but it was just here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please mark it with number 2, and mark the new church with number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the church here in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You said you knew that Vinko Martinovic's soldiers were covering the Bulevar between the medical centre and the memorial at Musala; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We worked in that area, and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please show the area on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think the witness ought to be given an opportunity to give a full answer to the questions. He's being cut off repeatedly now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm trying to conduct my cross-examination in a focused manner and to elicit from the witness answers which are as accurate and concise as possible. I'm not trying to lead the witness here. I'm just trying to get him to point out certain points in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, can you please point out in this photograph the area covered by Vinko Martinovic's soldiers. That's the area between the medical centre and the memorial at Musala.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can mark it out for you, the area in which I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you just about that particular area, the area you spoke about earlier. There's nothing else you need to circle here in the photograph. Please circle the area between the medical centre and the memorial at Musala. Get a felt pen and please circle it for me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you also mark the area into the depth too, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've only marked the front part, but I can circle the complete area. If you want me to, I can also mark the trenches that I was made to dig.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you just, please, complete the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you claim that this was the zone of responsibility of Vinko Martinovic's unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know really. The person who was in charge knows. But whenever we worked for Stela, they would bring us here, and then he would distribute us to different sectors. But they should know who was in charge of what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you only about your own knowledge, what you have personal knowledge of. The area you have just circled, was that the zone of responsibility of Vinko Martinovic's unit; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the usher please show the witness map 11.18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AF, take some time, have a look at this map, and try to get your bearings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this new map, please mark the same area that you've just marked off in that photograph. If you could just draw a circle around it again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I can manage with this one, because this is a different image and the lines drawn here are quite different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to or are you not able to? Please tell us. Can you please use this map to draw a circle around the same zone that you have just circled in the photograph, and show me the area controlled by Vinko Martinovic's unit. If you can't, just say so, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put the map away for the time being, but we may need them again, so it would be a good idea to keep them somewhere handy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that Luka Stojanovski took you to the headquarters, Stela's headquarters, and not to the engineering faculty on that particular day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would take us from the engineering faculty to wherever he had to take us to. He would bring us out of the camp. They would have us lined up. They would take us wherever, to Stela's place, or whatever needed to be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which unit was holding the area in which the engineering faculty was at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that Luka Stojanovski nearly always drove you to Vinko Martinovic's headquarters. Can you please describe for us the building where this headquarters was situated? How many floors did it have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but I know that Mr. Stela was in the second floor. How many floors it had exactly, I couldn't tell. It seemed more like a private house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell this Court: How many floors did the building have? If you can't, just say so, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure. Two floors, at least. It seemed more like Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. a private house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you that you were never either in front of that building or inside that building. Will you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I won't. You are just simply not right, and I find it impossible to agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why, then, are you not able to describe that building in detail, and you claim that you were brought -- that you were taken just in front of that building almost on a daily basis for a month or two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not answer my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What question? Can you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why are you not able to describe the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean? Sir, you asked me about the colour of the building. I can hardly remember the colour of my own building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. My apologies. I'll give up this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please bring back map 11.18 to show the witness. [In English] Mr. Usher, map 11.18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us try again with this map, Witness F. Can you show us on this map, show the Court, show all of us, the precise location of this building which you cannot describe but you know exactly where it is? So can you please point it out on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, Stela's building was here, and there was another one to the left of the roundabout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark the first spot you've just shown with number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can agree that what you marked with number 1 is the location of Vinko Martinovic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the other location you have indicated? Please mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this other location which you just marked with number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What am I supposed to show you now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it? What does this number 2 stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place I've marked as number 2, there was another headquarters, not Stela's, but another one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also taken to that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the same map, can you please indicate to us and mark as number 3 the precise location of the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which mark am I supposed to use?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please mark as number 4 the elementary school building that you've referred to, as well as the Kantarevac playground.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please show us, and just put an "X" there, the garage in which you said you spent some time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really show it to you on this map, because it's a very small area in the map. It was on the same plateau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it adjacent to this green area which we can see in the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what this green area stands for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just above number 3 and number 4, you just marked the big green area. You don't know what it stands for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, it's just a green area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. What exactly were you doing in that garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we were doing in that garage? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us, please, return to Luka Stojanovski. Yesterday you claimed that for a month or two you were brought -- you had been brought to the medical centre almost on a daily basis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he was always the one to drive you there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, always. And whenever we saw him in front of the camp, we knew immediately where we would be taken to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I put it to you that always, and without exception, he was the one to drive people from the Heliodrom to the Light Assault Brigade -- Battalion of the military police, but never took people to Vinko Martinovic's unit, what will you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who he was working as a driver for, whether for the military police or for Stela, but he was wearing military police insignia on his shoulder strap. And every time he took us for work, he was taking other persons too, and he would always be the one to come and pick us up. And whenever he showed up with an all-terrain vehicle, we knew where we would be taken to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree that you do not know who Luka Stojanovski was working as a driver for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose whoever needed persons for work, and whenever he was on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you again that he only worked as a driver for the 1st Light Assault Battalion of the military police but never for Stela's units. What will you tell me then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think you're wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please show the witness Exhibit 566.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, this is a list of inmates from the Heliodrom, with records of how the inmates were released, who took them away, and where to. So can you please open the page 01543659 [as interpreted]. You'll find it in the lower right corner. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 01543659 [as interpreted]. 01534659. 01534659. Can you please have a look at the following page also, last three numbers 660. What can you read there at the beginning? Will you agree that it reads "1st Light Assault Battalion of the military police"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at the other page now with 660 as the last three numbers. Who is supposed to provide the security? Can we agree that the name stated there is Luka Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 1543660 [as interpreted], just behind the name of the person marked as number 60 in the right column.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at page 0543648 and 015434648 [as interpreted]. Do you agree that the heading is "1st Light Assault Battalion of the military police"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only thing I can see here is the 1st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but look at the column to the right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. 1st Light Assault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you turn to the next page, please. The last three numbers are 650.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the column to the left, behind the name marked as number 80, Luka Stojanovski. Is that what it says in the column to the left? That's at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you looking at the page number 01543 -- 01534650? And then number 80, you can see "taken away by Luka Stojanovski," the left column at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us continue, please. Can you please turn to page number 01534612. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Can you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we just adjourn now, please, because I have a feeling that my client isn't really feeling too well, so maybe he should have his therapy now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Mr. President. That's only two minutes earlier, and I just want him to be able to last the afternoon session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.58 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. I noticed your client was not in the room. Are we going to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client was really feeling bad. He wasn't feeling well. So it would be better for him to be examined. This is obviously too lengthy for him, and but we'll try to continue so as not to disturb your schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Mr. Seric, please continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 566.2 is the document that is in front of the witness: Could you have a look at page 01534612.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What should I have a look at?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 01534612. In the left-hand column, can you see that it says "the 1st Light Assault Battalion of the military police," and at the bottom, after the name under number 15 it says "security, Luka Stojanovski"? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn the page now, 01535118. Can you see the date, the 31st of August, 1993? It's at the top of the left column. And also it says "the 1st Light Assault Brigade of the military police." And to the right, at the bottom, it says that "security was provided by Luka Stojanovski."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now could the Exhibit 661.1 be shown to the witness. 661.1. No, that's not it. That is not the exhibit. This is also the list of -- or the booklet of prisoners from the Heliodrom. 661.1. I could provide my copy. But for the sake of brevity -- I have a whole series of identical documents, so I will show the witness, in just one sentence, that in all of them, it says that Luka Stojanovski - and I've already shown this to the witness - that he only drove people from the Heliodrom for the 1st Light Assault Brigade of the military police, and not for any other unit. So I'm repeating this claim so that we don't have to go through all these documents. Allow me to finish, please. I repeat my claim that Luka Stojanovski only drove - and you yourself said that he was a military policeman - he only drove prisoners from the Heliodrom for the 1st Light Assault Battalion of the military police. He didn't drive for any other unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your response to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you are right, but Luka drove us wherever it was necessary to drive us. He would also drive us to Mr. Martinovic, and anywhere else when he was on shift. It wasn't every day, but when he was on shift, he would drive us, and he would drive us wherever it was necessary, down to Buna, Blagaj as well. I can't remember all the places. Up to Gubavica and elsewhere. He was the one who drove us, for the most part, to these places. I didn't say that he was Stela's soldier, that he drove for Stela, but he drove us where it was necessary. He drove people where it was necessary. And I never said that Luka Stojanovski was Mr. Martinovic's soldier. I said that he was a military policeman. I don't know which brigade he belonged to. That didn't interest me. I only know where he drove us and where we worked and where we moved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A short while ago you told us that Luka Stojanovski also took you to the building that was Vinko Martinovic's base, and you tried to describe this building to us. Is it correct to say that you said, just before the break, that the office was on the second floor of that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was on the second floor. That is certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to that office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I personally went there, and I sat in Mr. Martinovic's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that building only had one floor and that in the premises, in the rooms on that first floor, there were detainees in those rooms, what would you reply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I'm not familiar with that. I don't know whether someone slept there or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm telling you that that building only had one floor, and this has been confirmed by many witnesses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the building resembled a private house, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the office was on the second floor and that the building even had several floors.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I said that the gentleman was on the second floor. Whether there were any others, I don't know, but it did resemble a private house. I was personally present in the office with that gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other prisoners when you were there? What was on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't interested. I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many rooms were on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was that office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't very big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't right now. I don't remember. But I was sitting in that office with Mr. Martinovic. There was a young lady there, another colleague with me, and she served us with coffee. We were also given some cigarettes by Mr. Martinovic, and Mr. Martinovic even offered us some sort of cake or biscuit; it's not important. He then ordered the young lady who was with him to bring a sack of oranges or tangerines - I can't remember - so I could take them to other detainees down there. I did that. I took them to these people and they shared them out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Mr. Martinovic knows this man very well. If necessary, I will provide you with the name. If not --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Hasib Lulic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember the exact date, but it was sometime when we arrived there, in the morning to work, we were taken down there and two soldiers appeared to take charge of us, to take us to work in that street in Liska Park. So he recognised this person, this man, and he asked him, "What are you doing here?" I don't know what he replied. Apparently he said he had surrendered himself, and he replied, "Given the woods in Sovici, why did you surrender? Why didn't you flee?" He asked him to come to his office. I was with that man, and I went out together with him. As I said, we were sitting there together. We were offered cigarettes and other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the surroundings of that building in which you say Vinko Martinovic's units had their base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you explain to this Trial Chamber the fact that you don't remember anything, but you do remember the office on the second floor, and there was no such second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there was a second floor. It did exist. That's for sure. Because I remember very well that I went up the stairs, and the first floor doesn't have stairs, not according to any criteria.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm a bit hesitant to object. However, I do think it's necessary to suggest that the scope of this cross-examination is really beyond again what was the specific issue that the Trial Chamber authorised this rebuttal evidence. I would certainly have enjoyed the opportunity to go into these issues on the direct examination, because it's clear that the witness had very frequent contact with the ATG Vinko Skrobo. We didn't do that on direct examination because we felt ourselves bound by the parameters that the Trial Chamber had given in respect of this witness's testimony. Obviously, there are many -- a great number of many other relevant issues that he could have given direct evidence on but did not. These are clearly issues of relevance to the case that are being inquired into at this time by my learned friend. I just wish to point out that they were not gone into in any detail whatsoever on the direct exam because we felt that the Trial Chamber's rebuttal decision prevented us from doing that. I'd just merely mention that. I think obviously if the Trial Chamber wants to hear the evidence, we have no objection. It may, however, necessitate some re-direct on these issues which go beyond the issue of the burial that was the subject of the direct examination. We're also getting, if I could be candid, we're getting quite nervous over on this side about the time. We have again other rebuttal witnesses. We've been given a limited amount of time. We've lost a lot of time already, for a number of reasons, and that is something also that is of increasing concern on the Prosecution bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, I think you are entitled to ask some question to challenge the credibility of this witness, but the main issue here is the burial of Mr. Harmandzic. I hope you could lead this witness into that area as soon as possible, because we are only interested in this very issue in the rebuttal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, absolutely, Mr. President. However, this witness has never mentioned Nenad Harmandzic, believe it or not. He has spoken about everything, about the -- but he never mentioned this name. And I'm glad that I have the opportunity to tell my colleagues, the Prosecutors, that I was in the same position when cross-examining our witnesses as they were when they were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. cross-examining our witnesses. I'm glad to have been able to hear such an objection, because I want to say that I'm using the same method, the same style, that they employed when they were cross-examining our witness. We also had examinations in chief, and they did not relate to the subject of our cross-examination. They questioned witnesses about whatever they wanted to in their cross-examination. And as I want to show this witness that he is not at all definite when he speaks about where he was and what he did, and when I want to show that he's hesitant and not trustworthy, and when I prove this by using documents, et cetera, then I have the right to do this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm addressing the Trial Chamber. You're just a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not -- I don't speak the language. I don't know the tenor of what was just said to the witness by counsel, but it appears to me that counsel ought to address the witness with respect, the respect that he's entitled to. He's made statements about the witness and his views on the witness's credibility in the presence of the witness, and I think the witness is entitled to respond whether or not he's being directly addressed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, just said addressing the Trial Chamber: "You are just a witness here." I think the transcript, you know, picked up these words. But anyway, Mr. Seric, please move on. We have to finish this witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we will finish with the witness, but believe me, I want to take advantage -- I want to put all the questions that I planned to put in the course of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I tell you that we have documents in our possession with regard to taking prisoners away from the Heliodrom to do -- to carry out work and your name is mentioned in them too, but it never says that you were taken to see Vinko Martinovic, what would you -- what would your response be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not right, sir. If I hadn't been taken away, taken there, I wouldn't have been in his office with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show Exhibit P66.2 [As interpreted] again. I'm not sure. I think the witness might have it in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you have a look at page 01534600.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. What was the exhibit number again? I'm having trouble locating this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 566.2. We referred to it just a minute ago. The page number is 01534600.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the top of the right-hand column, it says "Engineers." Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't read this out aloud, but is your name, your first and last name, under number 16?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at page 01534608. 01534608. At the top of the right-hand column, does it say "Logistics"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name, is your first and last name, under number 5? In the right-hand column.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Have a look at page 01534622. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last three numbers are 622. In the left-hand corner, does it say "Logistics"? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your first and last names are under number 3; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at page 01534628.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If it would speed things along, we'll agree that the witness was taken out to work with these other units at the times indicated in this logbook. We think the logbook is accurate, and if his name appears as having been signed out to a particular unit on a particular day, we agree to it; we don't challenge it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, you know that this issue is not disputed, so there's no need to point to every place to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with you, Mr. President, and with my colleague Mr. Stringer. However, my question derives from all of this again. How is it that at no point in these documents which the Prosecution provided us with, at no point does it mention that this witness was taken to the Vinko Martinovic -- to Vinko Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain this to us? Can you or can't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you putting this question to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you should say so. Sir, you have found several lists here, and it doesn't say where we went exactly. I didn't say that we went out every day. We went there every day. Sometimes we went to other places, but on each occasion when we were taken to work, Mr. Stela or Mr. Martinovic never appeared. So on this list of prisoners who went to work, the person who came to collect them would always sign this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to say that what you are claiming is correct but not what it states, what these documents state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says in the documents, some parts of that are correct, but there are other parts which are not correct, because what I want to tell you, sir, is that when Mr. Luka would drive us to work, he would sign for us. When he would take us there and when he would take us back. But they never put down where the people were going to work, but they would say which battalion was delivering them and which battalion was taking them. It never said that we worked for this battalion or that battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I tell you that in these documents there is also a list of prisoners who were taken to Vinko Martinovic's unit, what would your response be to that? And they weren't taken to some other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't say anything. There were such details too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
